title: 国際情勢は歴史的変革期 政府方針
body:
政府は１０日、年内に改定する国家安全保障戦略で、国際情勢について「歴史的かつ根本的な変革期を迎えている」との認識を示す方針を固めた。安保環境では「六つの変容」が起きているとして、具体的には法の支配に基づく国際秩序の揺らぎや、ＡＩ（人工知能）による技術革新などを挙げた。新たな国家防衛戦略には、ＡＩを活用した意思決定の迅速化を盛り込む。【表】政府が示した国家安全保障戦略と国家防衛戦略の改定ポイント
２０２２年に改定された現行の３文書は、安保政策の指針となる国家安保戦略と自衛隊の能力に関する国家防衛戦略、整備する防衛体制や必要な金額を示す防衛力整備計画からなる。３文書改定に向けた与党の実務者協議の初会合で、政府側が両戦略を説明した。
国家安保戦略の改定ポイントでは、ロシアによるウクライナ侵略や、中国とロシアの連携、ロシアと北朝鮮の協力深化に加え、内向き志向を強める米国の外交政策などを例示した。その上で、紛争を解決するために「武力に訴えることに抵抗がなくなっていく危険」があると指摘した。
日本が直面する「六つの変容」は、▽法の支配に基づく国際秩序の根幹の揺らぎ▽ＡＩなどの技術革新▽新しい戦い方▽経済の武器化▽インド太平洋地域のパワーバランス▽国や社会のあり方――とした。厳しく複雑な状況下で抑止力を確保するために、外交力、防衛力、経済力、技術力、情報力、人材力の６本柱を「有機的に連携させる」と強調した。
日米同盟や同志国連携を通じた抑止力・対処力の強化も掲げた。経済安全保障の確保に向けては「集団的強靱（きょうじん）性」の考え方を盛り込み、中国を念頭に、経済的威圧に対して同志国で連携して対抗する方針だ。
国家防衛戦略の概要では、防衛力の基本的な考え方について「相手の目的達成を拒否する能力」を持つことで、侵攻を未然に防ぐ抑止力を高めることを目指す方針を明記した。無人機の活用や長射程ミサイルの運用など四つの能力と、人材や防衛産業など四つの基盤を強化し、陸海空の自衛隊の統合運用の強化を図る。

title: 北海道で史上最も早い-20℃以下
body:
今日11日(水)の朝は全国的に冷え込みが強く、午前6時までの最低気温は今季最も低い所が多くなっています。北海道の幌加内ではマイナス20.2℃と、全国で今季初めてマイナス20℃以下になり、アメダスが整備された1978年の統計以来、最も早い記録となりました。東京都心は5.1℃、名古屋6.5℃、大阪は7.9℃まで下がりました。通勤の際は冬のコートやマフラー、手袋など暖かい服装をご用意ください。
今日11日(水)は、強い寒気が流れ込んでいる中、晴れて放射冷却が強まり、全国的に寒い朝を迎えています。最低気温は今季これまでで最も低い所が多くなっています。午前6時までの最低気温は、北海道の幌加内でマイナス20.2℃と、全国で今季初めて20℃以下の気温を観測し、アメダスが整備された1978年の統計以来、最も早い記録となりました。最低気温が0℃未満の冬日となっている地点は全国の約3割にあたる262と、今季最多です。そのほか仙台は2.1℃、東京都心5.1℃、横浜6.7℃、名古屋6.5℃、大阪は7.9℃まで下がり、いずれも今季一番低い気温を更新しました。通勤の際は冬のコートやマフラー、手袋など暖かい服装をご用意ください。

title: ダンプカー衝突 自転車の男性重体
body: 11日朝、大分市の県道交差点で大型ダンプカーと自転車が衝突する事故があり、自転車に乗っていた高校生とみられる男性が意識不明の重体となっています。【写真をみる】事故直後の現場、ダンプカーの車体下に巻き込まれた自転車警察や消防によりますと、大分市下郡北の県道にある加納西交差点で11日午前8時20分ごろ、ダンプカー（10トン）と自転車が衝突しました。この事故で、自転車に乗っていた高校生とみられる男性が病院に運ばれましたが、意識不明の重体です。現場は信号機のある交差点で、自転車が道路の左側を直進していたところ、左折してきたダンプカーと衝突したとみられています。警察はダンプカーを運転していた大分市迫の会社員・永吉成美容疑者（61）を過失運転傷害の疑いで現行犯逮捕しました。また、重体となっている男性の身元確認を進めるとともに、事故の詳しい原因を調べています。

title: 前澤友作氏なぜ敗訴 詐欺広告裁判
body:
SNS上で著名人になりすます詐欺広告をめぐり、実業家の前澤友作氏がフェイスブックなどの運営会社を訴えた裁判で、東京地裁は10日、前澤氏の訴えを退けました。【動画】前澤氏「野放しOK？」詐欺広告めぐるメタ社などとの「1円訴訟」で敗訴
「毎日80万円を獲得」などと書かれた画像。実業家の前澤友作氏の名前や写真を勝手に使った「詐欺広告」です。ほかにも、着物姿の前澤氏に「無料投資教室を開きました」と書かれたものが、実際にSNSで流れていました。前澤友作氏（2024年）「悲しい。怒っています。ぶっちゃけ怒っています。何度も何度も、特にフェイスブックさんにはお伝えして、削除してください、改善してくださいと言っているけれども、一向に減らないどころか、むしろ増えている現状に、とても憤りを感じます」前澤氏は、2024年から、詐欺広告が流れたフェイスブックなどを運営するIT大手メタ社などを訴える裁判を起こしていましたが、10日、東京地裁は訴えを退けました。
どのような理由で、この判決にいたったのでしょうか。前澤氏の訴えは、詐欺広告が掲載されたことで、肖像権などが侵害されたとし、損害賠償と前澤氏の名前や肖像を使った、広告の掲載の差し止めを求めたものです。「お金が欲しいわけではなく、メタ社などの行為が違法なのか、合法なのかはっきりさせたい」としていて、求めた損害賠償額は、わずか1円でした。まず、東京地裁は、肖像権などが侵害されたという主張に対して、詐欺広告が肖像権の侵害に当たると、認めました。裁判長「本件広告が原告の肖像権を侵害する点について争いはない」
その上で、損害賠償については、「メタは広告の投稿自体に直接関与していないから、不法行為の責任を負うことはできない」などとし、請求を退けました。広告の掲載の差し止めについては、メタ社側が、詐欺広告のほとんどを2日以内で掲載停止にしていて、その対策を継続するとしていることから「差し止めの必要性は認められない」としました。判決を受けて、前澤氏は…前澤氏のXより「メタ側に、詐欺広告を発見・削除する義務はないとの判決。ってことは野放しでもOK？　ほんとにそれでいいのかな？　控訴を検討します」前澤氏の代理人弁護士によると、いまも、SNS上に前澤氏に関する詐欺広告が多く流れているということです。一方、メタ社は「判決を肯定的に受け止めている。詐欺広告に対処し、利用者の保護に引き続き取り組む」とコメントしています。

title: イベ閑散 主催は集客「約束せず」
body:
ホームページで「東軍vs西軍」などと大々的に紹介されていたのは、先週末、鳥取県で開催されたグルメイベントです。ただ、「5万人規模」としながら客はまばらで、複数の出店者から集客や設営に対する不満の声があがっています。主催者側が「news zero」の取材に答えました。【画像】“5万人規模”集客のはずが…鳥取で開催「食フェス」閑散　集客や設営に出店者から不満の声　主催者側の説明は
鳥取県倉吉市。この広い場所で週末、行われたのが…。イベントHPより「これは、ただの食フェスではない」「令和の関ヶ原」こう呼びかけたグルメイベント、「ローカル フード ファイト イン 鳥取」。北は北海道、南は沖縄県まで全国から出店者を集め、グルメ以外にも多くのショーを予定していたのが分かります。いま、このイベントをめぐり、波紋が広がっています。島根県松江市でからあげを販売する飲食店。グルメイベントに出店していましたが…。からあげ店 社長／グルメイベントに出店「これは全部鶏肉。（イベントに）出す予定だったムネ肉」およそ200キロの鶏肉を仕込んでいましたが、余ってしまったといいます。からあげ店 社長／グルメイベントに出店「5万人規模の集客という話と、去年の焼き鳥フェスで10万（人）近く来ているということで出店を決めた」
自然に囲まれ、レトロな町並みが広がる倉吉市。人口およそ4万2000人の町で、グルメイベントの主催者側には、過去の実績から「5万人の集客を見込む」と説明されたといいます。しかし出店者は、初日に来場したのは300人程度だったのではと話します。イベント2日目の午前中に撮影された会場の様子。たしかに写真では会場の広さに比べ、来場者は少ないようにみえます。出店者からは、来場者の規模感に加え、運営体制にも疑問の声が…。からあげ店 社長／グルメイベントに出店「当日行ったらテントがない。テーブル・イスが投げたまま、電気がきていない状態。まじで？大丈夫ですかこれ」出店者は、出店料として事前に5万5000円を主催者側に入金。ほかにも経費がかさみ、初日の売り上げは1万円ほど。翌日の出店をやめる事態になりました。

title: 日本のエンタメを排除 きしむ日中
body:
ハムスターに似たキャラクターが登場する日本アニメ「ちいかわ」が中国の若者らを魅了している。９月以降、北京や広東省で公式ショップがオープンし、週末はぬいぐるみなどを買い求める行列が店外へ続く。【図解】中国で停滞している日本のエンタメ事業や相互交流
上海でのフィギュア特別展では、３９０元（約９３００円）の入場券が開幕１週間前に完売した。大学院生の崔子軒さん（２５）は「心温まるストーリーで絵柄もかわいい」と語る。
日本食の中でコスパ（費用対効果）が良い店もデフレ下で人気だ。昨年１１月に日中関係が悪化した後も、回転ずしチェーン「スシロー」は新店舗を開き、平日に２時間超の順番待ちができる。
２０１２年、日本の沖縄県・尖閣諸島の国有化に中国政府が猛反発した際は中国で反日デモが起きた。群衆は日本料理店を壊し、電化製品をボイコットした。だが、現在は「政治状況と『自分が好きな日本』を区別する人たちが若者を中心に増えているようだ」と日本語教育に関わる中国人女性（４７）は話す。
多くの中国人が訪日し、日本観が多様化したことが変化の背景にあるとみられる。日本政府観光局（ＪＮＴＯ）の統計では、１２年以降に日本を訪れた中国人は延べ６５００万人に及ぶ。
こうした中国の「民意」に逆行するように、日本のエンタメ文化を排除する動きが続いている。
日本映画は、昨年１１月に日中関係が悪化した時点で公開中だったアニメ「鬼滅の刃」を最後に新たな封切りはなく、香港に渡航して「ちいかわ」の映画を見た女性（１８）は「中国本土の映画館で見ることができたらよかったのに」と漏らす。許認可を担う官庁や配給元が習近平（シージンピン）政権の中枢に忖度（そんたく）しているとの見方が強い。
日本の人気歌手のコンサートも中止されたままだ。東部の都市で昨年末、ある歌手の公演を企画した音楽関係者は公安当局から呼び出しを受けた。「いまの政治状況を見れば分かるだろう」。担当者はこう述べて暗に中止を求めた。

title: 米・露・ウの協議 9カ月ぶり再開
body: ロシアによるウクライナへの侵攻を巡り、米国、ウクライナ、ロシアの3カ国が10日、約9カ月ぶりに協議を再開した。米国は協議の焦点を両国間の停戦から欧州全体の安全保障に広げ、交渉を動かそうとしているが、各国が折り合える着地点は見通せない。【写真】米特使のウィトコフ特使ら=ロイター。3者協議にも出席した3カ国の代表団は、アラブ首長国連邦（UAE）の首都アブダビで11日まで協議を実施する予定。協議の冒頭で、ロシア代表団を率いるメジンスキー大統領補佐官は「平和に向けた前進につながることを期待する」と述べた。3カ国による協議は今年1～2月にも計3回開いたが、領土の扱いなど主要争点で大きな前進はなかった。米イスラエルがイランを攻撃した2月末以降は、米政権の外交上の優先課題がイラン情勢に移り、協議は事実上中断していた。その後、9月に米特使のウィトコフ氏がモスクワとキーウを相次いで訪問。両国首脳に対し、3カ国協議を再開したい意向を示した。11月の中間選挙を控えたトランプ政権には成果を急ぐ思惑もあったとみられ、協議再開に向けた調整が急ピッチで進められた。米代表団の一人であるウィトコフ特使は、11月2日のSNSへの投稿で、今回の協議の焦点は「戦後の安全保障」などになると表明した。

title: G7外相会合 ウ支援で声明公表へ
body:
【パリ＝福田麻衣、上地洋実】パリで開かれていた先進７か国（Ｇ７）外相会合は１０日、２日間の議論を終えて閉幕した。ロシアの侵略を受けるウクライナ支援について協議し、冬季を乗り越えるために必要なエネルギー支援に取り組み、完全な停戦を実現することの重要性を確認した。同日中にも共同声明を公表する見通しだ。【写真】Ｇ７外相会合に臨む茂木外相
閉幕後、茂木外相は記者団の取材に「Ｇ７を含む国際社会と連携をしてウクライナ支援、そして公正かつ永続的なウクライナの平和の実現に向けて取り組んでいきたい」と強調した。１０日の会合ではイラン情勢についても議論し、Ｇ７外相はイランが事実上封鎖しているホルムズ海峡で自由で安全な航行を確保する重要性を確認し、通航料の徴収に反対する立場を共有した。
議長国フランスによると、Ｇ７各国は共同声明の公表に向け、最終調整を続けている。

title: 米国防長官に弾劾決議案 何が問題
body:
米共和党のマシー下院議員は11月9日、ヘグセス国防長官への弾劾訴追決議案を提出した。議会の承認を得ない対イラン戦争など8項目で、憲法・連邦法違反を追及する。中間選挙で共和党が大敗した直後の動きだ。現在の下院では共和党が僅差で多数派を占めるが、民主党が結束し、共和党から数人が賛成に回れば、出席状況によっては訴追が成立する可能性がある。ただし、訴追されても直ちに罷免されるわけではない。何が問題なのか。追及の中身と今後の焦点を整理する。
米共和党のマッシー下院議員（ケンタッキー州）は9日、ヘグセス国防長官の弾劾を求める決議案を提出した。出典：TBS CROSS DIG with Bloomberg　2026/11/10(火)
ヘグセス氏の弾劾訴追には、下院の過半数の賛成しか必要としないため、訴追に必要な票数は集まる可能性が高い。出典：CNN.co.jp　2026/11/10(火)
決議案は11日までに下院で採決などの対応が行われる見通しで共和党の一部議員が賛成に回る可能性もあるということです。出典：FNNプライムオンライン　2026/11/10(火)
ただ、ヘグセス長官の罷免（ひめん）には上院で3分の2の賛成が必要になるため、弾劾の実現は困難とみられています。出典：テレ朝NEWS　2026/11/10(火)
決議案の8項目中3項目は、イラン戦争を巡るものだ。議会の承認を得ずに戦争を始め、議会が戦闘の終結か承認の取得を求めた後も作戦を続けたと主張する。原則60日以内の戦闘終結を義務づける戦争権限法の期限にも違反したと指摘する。
ほかに、麻薬密輸の疑いがある船舶への攻撃、ベネズエラのマドゥロ氏の拘束、議会未承認のイエメンでの軍事作戦、民間人を守るための法令の軽視などがある。いずれも決議案が指摘する疑惑で、違法性が確定したわけではない。
核心は、大統領の命令を実行する長官が憲法や法律を守ったかどうかだ。政策への不満を超え、弾劾に値する権限乱用があったかを議会が判断する。ヘグセス氏は政治的な攻撃だと反発している。
下院では米国時間11日までに決議案への対応を巡る採決が必要とされる。ただし、共和党指導部が委員会付託や決議案を退ける動議によって、訴追の採決を阻む可能性もある。
訴追には下院の過半数、罷免には上院の出席議員の3分の2の賛成が必要だ。共和党からの造反の規模と、トランプ氏が長官を支え続けるかが焦点となる。訴追が成立しても、上院での審理は民主党が上下両院の多数派となる来年1月以降に持ち越される可能性がある。

title: 米国防長官 自身への弾劾「茶番」
body: Phil Stewart[ワシントン １０日 ロイター] - ヘグセス米国防長官は１０日、イラン紛争を巡り、自身に対する弾劾に向けた動きについて、「茶番」で、‌敵対勢力の思惑に利用される「妨害行為だ」と非難し⁠た。共和党のマッシー下院議員は９日、議会の承認なしにイランとの戦争を遂行したことや、職権乱用などの容疑を巡り、ヘグセス長官に​対する８項目の弾劾訴追条項を提出した。ヘグセス長官は５月以来となる国防総省での記者会見で、トランプ大統領に対‌する過去の弾劾は失敗に終わり、「トランプ氏はより強くなり、米国民によって再選された」と指摘。「今回もまた失敗に終わるだろう。‌トランプ大統領を支持すること‌で、私がトランプ氏と同じ側になるのであれ​ば、私は喜んでいつでもその立場を受け入れる」と語った。弾劾に向けた動きは「愛‌国心ではない。破壊行為だ」と批判。「われわれの敵にプロパガンダ上の勝利を与えることになる」‌との認識を示した。イランの戦争​については「これら作戦全てを支持する。作戦を実行‌できたことを誇りに思っている」と述べた。イラン戦争が、米中間選挙での共和党の⁠敗因の一つだったというバンス副大統領の発言については、紛争から教訓を学ぶとしつつも、「イランが核兵器を保有しないことを確実にするという正当な理由に基⁠づいて行われた」と擁護した。マッシー下院議員​はＸへの投稿で、下院が１０日‌に弾劾決議案に関する手続き上の動議について最初の採決を行うと明らかにした。トランプ大統領は自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」へ⁠の投稿で、マッシー議員を非難した上で、ヘグセス氏の対応を「Aプラ⁠ス、プラス、プラスの評価に値する」とし、同長官への支持を再表明した。バンス米副大⁠統領は公の場で戦争に疑問を呈し、共和党が中間選挙で大敗した原因だと指摘してき‌たが、１０日はヘ⁠グセス氏への支持を表明。Ｘに「これはイランの問題ではない。ピート（​ヘグセス氏）が国防総省の官僚組織に立ち向かったことが問題にされている」と投稿した。

title: 障害者雇用ビジネス 登録制を検討
body:
障害者の働く場所を雇用企業に提供する障害者雇用ビジネスを巡り、厚生労働省は不適切な業者への規制強化に向け、「登録制」の導入の検討に乗り出した。当初は「届け出制」を導入する方向だったが、事業の適正化を強く促すには国が悪質な業者を排除できる登録制が必要だと判断した。【表】障害者雇用促進法の改正で想定される登録制と届け出制の内容
厚労省は、１１日に開かれる労働政策審議会（厚労相の諮問機関）の分科会で登録制の案を示す。
現状では雇用ビジネスの規制はない。厚労省は８月末に公表した法規制案で、不適切な事案が確認された業者に指導や勧告ができるよう、業者の事業開始時に国への届け出を義務付ける制度の創設を提案していた。
届け出制では、国は業者の事業要件を確認することはなく、事業停止などの行政処分を科すこともできない。厚労省は相次ぐ雇用ビジネスの不適切な事案を受け、業者の登録に際して事業要件を確認し、登録の取り消しなどの処分も可能になる制度を導入すべきだと方針転換した。
さらに、監督強化に向け、業者に定期的な業務報告や登録更新などを義務付けることも視野に入れている。こうした新たな規制策を盛り込んだ障害者雇用促進法改正案を、来年の通常国会に提出することを目指す。
雇用ビジネスを巡っては、業者の「サンクスラボ」（那覇市）を介して大手企業などに雇われた一部の障害者が実質的な仕事を与えられず、精神的苦痛を受けるなどしたほか、別の業者の拠点で働いていた障害者が労災認定を受けた事例も判明している。

title: タマホーム社員 保険金を不正請求
body:
損害保険大手各社が、保険金不正請求問題で再び大きく揺れている。震源は注文住宅大手のタマホームだ。同社は保険代理店事業も手掛けており、損保各社から委託を受けて火災保険などを顧客に販売(募集)している。【詳報】タマホームで保険金不正請求発覚で大揺れの損害保険大手､第二の｢ビッグモーター事件｣となるか複数の関係者によると、保険募集の資格を持つタマホームの一部社員は、過去に使用した住宅の内装や設備における損傷箇所の画像を使い回すなどして、事故を捏造し火災保険金を請求したり、損傷を過大に見せて水増し請求したりしていた疑いがあるという。
■不正請求は損保3社で200件以上か遅くとも2020年から不正請求の疑いがあり、現時点での疑義件数は取引のある損害保険ジャパン、三井住友海上火災保険、東京海上日動火災保険の3社で合計200件以上に上るようだ。3社は目下、詳細な実態調査を進めており件数は今後さらに膨らむ可能性がある。損保各社が自社の火災保険をタマホームに優先して取り扱ってもらえるように、不正請求に目をつぶるような対応をしていた場合は、「ビッグモーター事件」とまさに同じ構図となり、大きな問題に発展しそうだ。
本記事はダイジェスト版です。不正請求の具体的な手口や詳細については、東洋経済オンライン有料版「タマホームで保険金不正請求が発覚で大揺れの損害保険大手、第二の「ビッグモーター事件」となるかでご覧いただけます。

title: SBGが7680億円の赤字 中間決算
body: ソフトバンクグループが10日発表した9月中間連結決算（国際会計基準）は、純損益が7680億円の赤字に転落した。【ひと目でわかる】ソフトバンクグループの連結純損益（2026年5月配信）前年同期は2兆9240億円の黒字だった。中間決算で赤字に陥ったのは3年ぶり。米国で進めている人工知能（AI）向けデータセンター事業を巡り、発電関連設備の調達計画を見直した影響で5972億円の損失を計上した。全体の投資利益は1兆7257億円と、前年同期から2兆円超減少した。後藤芳光専務は「昨年は最高に近い数字だ。1．7兆円は評価できる」と話した。新興企業などに投資する「ソフトバンク・ビジョン・ファンド」の投資利益は3412億円と、前年同期の10分の1に縮小した。対話型AI「チャットGPT」を手掛ける米オープンAIへの投資については、300億ドル（約4兆7000億円）の追加出資を10月に完了。累計出資額は646億ドル（約10兆円）に膨らみ、持ち分比率は約13％に上昇した。後藤氏はオープンAIに関し、「順調に推移している。AIの中長期的な視点から引き続き期待している」と述べた。サイバー攻撃の急増でAIに対する懸念が広がっていることについて、後藤氏は「いろいろな目でAIを見る時期が来ている。ただ、中長期的には大きなプラスになるだろう」との見解を示した。

title: トヨタ 軽トラックを米国で販売へ
body: ■ ダイハツの軽トラ「ハイゼットトラック ジャンボ」が、トヨタの新ブランド「サイオン」の1号車に【画像】中嶋副社長は米国の低速車両（LSV：Low-Speed Vehicle）のルールに従って軽トラックを導入するという。米国ではピックアップトラックが人気で、25年以上前の軽トラックが日本から輸入される米国市場の特性に対応していくトヨタ自動車の米国法人であるToyota Motor North America（TMNA）は11月10日（現地時間）、米国に新たな選択肢として新ブランド「Scion by Toyota（サイオン・バイ・トヨタ）」を立ち上げると発表した。サイオンは、かつて2003年に若年層向けのこれまでにない商品やビジネスを試行することを目標にスタート。100万台以上のサイオン車が販売され、このうち70％がトヨタの新規顧客となり、サイオンユーザーの半数が35歳を下まわるという、トヨタの可能性を広げたブランドだった。2016年8月に「若いお客様を惹きつける目標を達成できた」と、一定の成果を上げて「FR-S」「iA」「iM」などはトヨタブランドに移行。日本でも特に「bB」（サイオン「xB」）などは、サイオンでも売られたクルマとして知られていた。今回のサイオンブランド復活にあたっては、「好奇心、新たな可能性、そして新しい方法でモビリティを探求する自由を軸とする新ブランド」と位置付けており、ブランド初の車両として軽トラック（超小型ユーティリティトラック）「KEI-01」を発表した。KEI-01は、ダイハツ工業の「ハイゼットトラック ジャンボ」そのもので、日本のダイハツ九州 中津工場で生産後、バラバラの部品を米国に輸出し、米国のToyota Motor Manufacturing Indiana（トヨタ・モーター・マニュファクチャリング・インディアナ、以下インディアナ工場）で組み立てる。いわゆるセミノックダウン生産（Semi Knock Down、SKD）を行ない、2027年後半から組み立てを開始する予定。トヨタはこの取り組みのため、3400万米ドルを投資し、約50人の新規雇用を創出する。■ KEI-01の販売についてKEI-01の販売は特定のニーズに応える少量販売モデルとして、法人・事業者向けの試行プログラムを通じて提供していく。米国のユーザーニーズや使用実態を把握し、最適な提供方法を検討することを目的にしている。初期のフリート販売は、既存のトヨタ販売店から選定するScion by Toyota販売店を通じて行ない、各販売店が窓口となる。今後、市場動向、需要、事業運営上の条件を踏まえ、台数を限定した一般向け販売も検討する可能性がある。このKEI-01はScion by Toyotaのビジョンを初めて具現化したモデルとして位置付け、日本の軽トラックが培ってきた機能性、効率性、多用途性を備えた実績あるコンセプトを、トヨタグループならではのかたちで米国に届ける。米国の低速車両（LSV：Low-Speed Vehicle）に適用される連邦安全基準への適合を目指して設計、660cc 3気筒エンジン、無段変速機（CVT）、四輪駆動（4WD）を標準装備。買いやすい価格、高い実用性能、優れた小回り性能を兼ね備えるという。KEI-01は、米国の低速車両（LSV）に適用される連邦自動車安全基準（FMVSS）第500号への適合を目指して設計し、ステアリング位置は日本同様の右ハンドル車。最高速度は時速25マイル（約40km/h）とする予定で、LSVのルールに従った車両になる。州によっては公道を走行することもできるが、公道を走行できない州もあり、「手頃な価格の都市部向け商用車を求める小規模事業者」「日々の作業で頼りになる車両を必要とする農家や牧場経営者」「効率的な業務用車両を求める自治体、大学、企業の構内・事業所」「都市部で活動する配送・サービス事業者」「多用途に使える車両を求めるアウトドア愛好家や趣味を楽しむ方々」などのユーザーを想定している。サイオン・バイ・トヨタの立ち上げにあたっては、KEI-01のほか「SxS Concept（サイド・バイ・サイド コンセプト）」と「BKE Concept（バイク コンセプト）」を発表。サイド・バイ・サイドは、米国でATV（All Terrain Vehicle）やROV（Recreational Off-highway Vehicle）と呼ばれているジャンルの製品で、オフロード向けの四輪バギー。トヨタ自動車はレクサスブランドで「ROV CONCEPT」を開発していたが、サイオンのサイド・バイ・サイドでは、トヨタ タコマ ハイブリッドなどに採用されている直列4気筒2.4リッターターボエンジン＋1モーターハイブリッドのパワートレーン「i-FORCE MAX」を搭載。2.4リッターターボの豊かなトルク、電動モーターならではのレスポンスと静かさなどを活かした新世代のバギーになっている。バイク コンセプトは、豊田章男会長がWRC ラリージャパンやモビリティショーで乗る姿を見かけた二輪電動バイクを発展させたような電動バイク。折りたたみが可能で、サスペンションを持つオンロード仕様となっている。トヨタではオフロード向けに、前二輪、後一輪のランドホッパーを2027年以降に発売としているが、オンロード用、二輪ということで違う用途の電動バイクとなる。米国では、低層ビルディングを何棟にもわたって展開する企業も多く、そうした企業敷地や工場内の移動、豊田章男会長が度々使っているようにレース場などクローズドエリアでの移動などに向くモビリティと言えるだろう。トヨタ自動車代表取締役副社長 中嶋裕樹氏は、米国ミシガン州デトロイトでサイオン・バイ・トヨタの立ち上げを発表するとともに「KEI-01」をお披露目。サイオンのブランドコンセプトである「BEYOND START HERE」を紹介し、この発表から新たな動きが始まることを伝えた。

title: もう終わりやで 明石ダコ深刻不漁
body:
「もう、明石のタコは終わりやで」。兵庫県明石市の名産「明石ダコ」が、深刻な不漁に見舞われている。2015年に1046トンあった漁獲量は、2025年には124トンと約9割も減少。瀬戸内海の漁師からは「息子に漁業を継がせたくない」という悲痛な声まで聞こえてくる。一方、タコの採捕が制限される海では、ルールを十分に理解しないまま釣りに訪れる若者もいる。かつて豊かな漁場として知られた瀬戸内海で、何が起きているのか。関係者を取材した。【画像】見た目も食感もタコ? 価格高騰で注目される“代替品”
「もう、明石のタコは終わりやで」兵庫県明石市の漁協関係者は、地元の海の変化をそう嘆いた。明石海峡の激しい潮にもまれて育つマダコ、通称「明石ダコ」は、身が引き締まったブランド食材として知られる。地元名物の明石焼きにも使われているが、近年は深刻な不漁が続いている。明石市の集計によると、2015年に1046トンあったマダコの漁獲量は、2021年に133トンまで減少。その後、一時は回復したものの、2024年の231トンから2025年には124トンと再びほぼ半減した。明石以外でもタコの不漁が報じられているほか、円安や海外産地の漁獲動向などの影響で輸入タコも高騰している。庶民の味である「たこ焼き」の相次ぐ値上げも報じられている。「ここ最近、タコ漁のために港から出ている船は毎日5隻から多くても10隻ほどですが、30年ほど前は毎日20隻は軽く超えていました。平成から令和に変わった頃かな。ぐんと漁獲量が減って、苦しくなってきました」（同・漁協関係者）不漁は地元の食文化にも影を落としているという。明石焼きは、地元では「玉子焼き」とも呼ばれる郷土料理だ。今年10月には、1952年創業の老舗明石焼き店「よこ井」が74年の歴史に幕を下ろした。閉店は女将の引退によるものと報じられており、タコの不漁が直接の原因と確認されたわけではない。一方、漁協関係者はこう話す。「タコもこれだけ希少化していますからね。他にも臨時休業している老舗店があります。タコの減少が店の営業に影響していることは、漁協関係者の間でもよく知られています」漁師たちが不漁に頭を抱える一方、明石の海では別の問題も起きていた。明石市沿岸ではタコの資源を守るため、一般の釣り人にも採捕のルールが設けられている。共同漁業権が設定された区域では、定められた条件に違反してタコを採捕すると、漁業権侵害として100万円以下の罰金が科される可能性がある。前出の漁協関係者は話す。「毎年ルールが変わるので、知らないうちに違反している釣り人もいると思います。地元では、見かけない顔の人が禁止期間に釣具を持って歩いていたら、声をかけて注意することもあります」なお、タコの採捕ルールは年によって見直されることがあり、陸からの釣りと船からの釣りでも条件が異なる。「本音を言うと、私たち漁協関係者も毎年改定されるルールを覚え直すのが大変で疲弊しています」（同・漁協関係者）

title: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says
summary: The US Department of Justice says the men were involved in a string of plots, including a major incident near the UK airbase that is used by US armed forces.
body:
The US removed all its bombers from the UK's RAF Fairford base last month after a major incident in September that police described as "suspicious"
The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has announced charges against three Iran-backed operatives that it alleges were involved in a string of plots in the US and Europe.
The DOJ said Iranian agents most recently "orchestrated a terrorist plot at an air force base in the United Kingdom", saying they were involved inthe major incident in September near RAF Fairfordin the UK, where US armed forces were stationed.
One man, a dual Iranian-Iraqi national, is accused of communicating with contacts in the UK from a prison in New York where he is awaiting trial on previous charges. The other two are accused of doing the same from Iran.
Iran has strongly denied any involvement in the RAF Fairford incident, which came to light when suspicious vans were reported near the base. Seven men have been arrested in the UK over the incident.
Iranian Mohsen Mohajeri, Iraqi national Mohammad Ali al-Hassani and dual Iranian-Iraqi citizen Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi were charged in an indictment unsealed on Tuesday, the DOJ said.
It accuses the trio of planning attacks in Europe that were carried out under the name of a purportedly new group with the pseudonym Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (The Islamic Movement of the People of the Right Hand - HAYI).
"Of the 18 terrorist attacks in the spring of 2026 for which HAYI claimed responsibility in Europe, seven took place in the UK," the DOJ statement said. It added that the attacks involved "arsons, explosives, and in one instance, a near-fatal stabbing in London of two Jewish men, including a dual US-British citizen".
Two Jewish men were stabbed in Golders Green, north London, in April. A suspect is due to stand trial next year.
"This eight-count indictment shows the determination of Iran to commit terrorist attacks in Europe and the US," FBI Director Kash Patel said.
He added that one of the three "allegedly sent coded messages to assist in future acts of violence" from detention.
Patel said the accused were involved in nearly 20 attempted attacks in support of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and the Iran-backed Iraqi militia Kataib Hezbollah.
Armed police officers were posted outside the RAF Fairford base following the incident in September
A major incidentwas declared on 27 Septembernear the UK's RAF Fairford base, in the Cotswolds in Gloucestershire, after three suspicious vans were seen near the airbase.
No explosive materials were found in the vans, but a quantity of petrol was seized.
The DOJ said that in August, al-Hassani "allegedly directed and paid associates" in the UK to "conduct preparatory steps and arrange logistics for the RAF Fairford terrorist plot".
On 22 August, al-Hassani paid one individual to "perform pre-operational surveillance of RAF Fairford's perimeter", the department said.
In September, al-Hassani paid several people to help him prepare for the plot, the DOJ also alleged.
According to its statement, this included "procuring vans and barrels of fuel, researching the purchase of chemical accelerants, including large quantities of potassium chloride, and purchasing metallic objects that could be used as explosive shrapnel".
The suspects then gave the vans an appearance of being used by a fuel delivery business and a swimming pool supply business, the DOJ stated.
"On 26 September, al-Hassani allegedly tasked individuals to drive three vans, some of which were later determined to contain barrels of fuel, to the RAF Fairford base."
The DOJ also said al-Hassani was "in frequent communication" with the van drivers and helped to direct them where to drive.
"At least two of the three vans, while en route to the perimeter of RAF Fairford, encountered a security roadblock and were not allowed to proceed on their intended route," it added.
It was in the very early hours of 27 September, that the vans were spotted by a local farmer who was heading home from a party, and called the police.
What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe
The Iranian embassy in London has said it "categorically rejects and strongly condemns" what it called "unfounded and malicious speculations" linking Iran to the incident.
Two British nationalsappeared in court last monthin connection with the alleged Iran-linked plot.
The USwithdrew all its bombers from RAF Fairfordafter the incident, with President Donald Trump citing "some threats" to the base as the reason.
RAF Fairford has been used by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades.
In recent months, the US has flown B-1 and B-52 bombers from there to the Middle East for "defensive" strikes on Iran.
In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".

title: US Army soldier suspected of spying for Russia arrested in UK
summary: The 41-year-old senior soldier is accused of national security offences and is being questioned in London.
body:
The BBC understands the man was based at Imjin Barracks in Gloucestershire
A soldier in the US Army has been arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia, British counter-terror police have said.
The 41-year-old senior serviceman was arrested near Gloucester on Tuesday.
Counter Terrorism Policing London said the man had been arrested under section one and section three of the National Security Act 2023.
Section one of the Act relates to obtaining or disclosing protected information, while section three relates to assisting a foreign intelligence service.
As part of the investigation, officers are carrying out searches at two locations in Gloucestershire.
The BBC understands the soldier was based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire. The barracks serve as the headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC),a strategic operational base for the alliance.
Counter Terrorism Policing said it was not linked to any other ongoing investigations.
FBI director Kash Patel said in a statement: "This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies."
He added: "While this investigation is continuing, I want to send a clear message – this FBI has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners."
Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, from Counter Terrorism Policing London, described the arrest as "significant".
"The allegations are serious and our investigation is very much ongoing," she said.
The unnamed soldier is currently in custody at a London police station.
He has been detained under the National Security Act 2023, allowing police to hold him without charge for up to 14 days.
Brig Gen Sean Stinchon, commanding general of US Army Counterintelligence Command, said: "The alleged conduct of a senior soldier, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent.
"I encourage anyone who thinks they've witnessed something suspicious to report it to their local counterintelligence office."
Additional reporting by Daniel Sandford, UK correspondent.

title: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, for now
summary: Trump welcomes the outcome, praising Hegseth as a "Great American Patriot", but Democrats can try again next year.
body:
Watch: Republicans vote to block Hegseth impeachment from reaching full vote
An effort to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging war on Iran without congressional authorisation, has failed on Capitol Hill.
A majority of the House of Representatives agreed to refer impeachment articles to a committee - essentially killing the effort introduced by dissident Republican congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky - for now.
In his first news briefing from the Pentagon in six months, Hegseth called the impeachment effort a "farce" and "sabotage".
The bid to find the cabinet secretary guilty of misconduct and ultimately remove him from office was seen as a long shot as it could have required a number of other Republicans to defy President Donald Trump.
Massie was the only Republican to vote against moving the resolution to the Republican-led House Judiciary Committee on Tuesday.
His effort failed in a 211-204 vote, with more than a dozen members, including 11 Democrats, missing the vote.
The move to send the measure to the panel effectively kills the effort, as there is only a short period of time left in this Congress before Democrats take control in January.
President Trump celebrated the vote in a post on Truth Social, saying the effort "has miserably FAILED".
"Again, Victories in Venezuela and Iran, the Best Recruitment Numbers in the History of the Military (Long waiting lists to get in!), and Spirit like rarely seen before, led to the EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot," Trump said, referring to Hegseth.
Massie had previously acknowledged his impeachment bid may not succeed immediately, but argued it could help push Trump to replace Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process.
Hegseth: Impeachment effort is "farce" and "stunt"
The Kentucky congressman also said that removing Hegseth now would give the Senate time to approve a replacement while Republicans were still in power.
Impeachment resolutions can be carried past the end of a congressional term, meaning Democrats would be able to take it up next year.
The Democrats will take control of both chambers of Congress in January following a successful midterm election that allowed them control of both chambers.
House Speaker Mike Johnson, a Republican, had predicted earlier in the day that the impeachment bid would fail.
In the eight articles of impeachment formally introduced in the House on Monday, Massie said Hegseth was "breaking the law and must be held accountable" for fighting a war in Iran for more than 90 days without lawmakers' approval.
The impeachment articles also accused Hegseth of overseeing "extrajudicial killings" in the US campaign against boats alleged to be carrying drugs in the Pacific  Ocean and Caribbean Sea.
At a news conference on Tuesday, Hegseth called efforts to impeach him a political stunt by a Trump administration opponent who was "disgruntled and defeated".
Hegseth also argued Massie's resolution endangered national security, because it communicated to US adversaries "that the United States will actually punish its own warriors and its own civilian leadership for successfully executing lawful military operations".
"This is not patriotism. This is sabotage," he said.
He echoed some statements Trump had made during a surprise appearance at the White House briefing room on Monday, including touting a rise in military recruitment levels.
But Hegseth said Massie was motivated by policy differences and "not high crimes, not misdemeanours, not treason, not bribery, not the kinds of offences the founders intended when they wrote the impeachment clause".
Massie, who lost re-election earlier this year to a Trump-backed opponent, has been critical of Trump and the war in Iran since it began in February.
He had already incurred the president's ire for demanding the Trump administration release files on deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
While Hegseth has survived politically for now, many lawmakers - including some Republicans - have questioned how long he can last in the administration.
Texas Senator Ted Cruz, a Republican, said on Tuesday he expected Hegseth to resign or be fired by Trump.

title: Meghan's father Thomas Markle back in federal custody after allegedly removing ankle monitor
summary: The 82-year-old was placed under house detention in Florida last week after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material.
body:
Thomas Markle was placed under house detention at his assisted living facility in Florida last week
Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is back in federal custody in Florida after allegedly removing his ankle monitor, according to court documents.
Markle appeared before a federal magistrate judge in the Florida city of Tampa on Tuesday and was denied bond. Prosecutors say he removed the monitor early that morning.
US Judge Lindsay S Griffin found on Tuesday that Markle had violated the conditions of his pretrial release, court documents show.
Markle, who has denied possessing images of child sex abuse, was arrested in Florida last week and placed under house detention. He was also ordered to wear a location monitoring device.
The BBC has contacted his representatives.
Griffin described Markle's housing situation as "untenable", writing in the order revoking his pretrial release that "based on the lack of suitable housing, no condition or combination of conditions would reasonably assure the safety of any other person or the community and the defendant's appearance in court".
He also ordered a medical evaluation for Markle and said he "must receive all necessary and prescribed medication unless discontinued by a physician".
"Release conditions are court orders, not suggestions," Bill Essayli, the US attorney for Central California, wrote on X on Tuesday.
"We will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law," he added.
Markle, 82, was first arrested last week after the FBI, acting on warrants, searched storage units in Los Angeles registered to him which he had rented since 2008, with the last payment being made in October this year, the DoJ said.
Inside the units the FBI says agents seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material.
Witnesses "positively identified" Markle in two of the images believed to contain child sex abuse material.
In those images, the man pictured "appears to be in the age range of 30s to 40s", which suggests the alleged abuse dates back decades as Markle is currently 82 years old.
Markle appeared in court last week following his arrest. No plea was taken during the appearance, which set several conditions for his pretrial release, including that he be kept in home detention.
He is charged with one count of possessing indecent images of children, according to the DoJ.
FBI director Kash Patel said last week that Markle "allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions".
Markle has called the allegations "sick lies".
He moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and lived in Cebu until May. He was reportedly learning to walk again in Florida after having his leg amputated.
The duchess has been estranged from her father since 2018.The BBC understandsshe broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.
In a previously shared statement, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."
She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

title: 'It can kill us': Kenyans fear impact of El Niño with floods predicted
summary: Forecasters warn that this year's El Niño could be one of the strongest on record, with heavy rain and flooding in Kenya.
body:
Agnes Shikoli says she fears either drowning, or being crushed by her house
"It flooded up to here in March," Agnes Shikoli says, pointing to a spot halfway up the six-foot [1.8m] corrugated iron wall of her home in Kibera, one of the largest informal settlements in Kenya.
Her tiny house lies just a couple of metres from the Ngong river, which runs through this densely populated area in the capital, Nairobi.
The scars of floods in the long rainy season earlier this yearcan still be seen - including a broken TV in the corner which was immersed in water.
Tucked out of sight is a photo of her sister Beatrice Khalayi, 58, who died when intense rains caused widespread destruction in Kibera. She was among more than 60 people across the country who lost their lives.
"Someone called me to tell me that she had died of electrocution after her house flooded," Shikoli recalls. "When I see a picture of her, I feel uneasy, that's why I keep it far from me, so I don't see it."
With Kenya's short rainy season now starting, Shikoli tells the BBC she is afraid – especially following warnings that the El Niño weather phenomenon could bring a new round of flooding.
"I feel like it can kill us. These houses aren't made of stone," says the 62-year-old. "They can fall on us, or the water can drown us."
Kibera - and Kenya more widely - are on the frontline of preparations for the potential impact of El Niño.
Forecasters have warned that this year could see one of the strongest on record, bringing extreme weather to many parts of the world.
In southern Kenya, that means the threat of rains even more intense than usual.
Outside Shikoli's house, groups of men and women wearing high-visibility vests are shovelling and raking garbage out of the riverbed and disposing it far from the water.
This programme called Climate Worx, under the office of President William Ruto, is meant to rehabilitate Nairobi's rivers. Such exercises have intensified since Augustwhen warnings increased about the possible scale of this year's El Niño.
Rubbish clogging Nairobi's drains and sewers was seen as a major factor in the deadly floods earlier this year
Similar work to unclog drainage systems is ongoing across Nairobi, a sprawling city built on hilly ground crossed by three major rivers.
But the workers have a huge task on their hands.
Blocked drains and inadequate sewage systems were widely blamed for the high number of deaths after the floods earlier in the year, as the excess rainfall had nowhere to escape.
The Nairobi County disaster management chief, Bramwell Simiyu tells the BBC that drainage systems have been "untouched for many years" and that removing the rubbish from them will save lives.
Floods disproportionately affect informal settlements in Nairobi, especially those near rivers, like Kibera and Mathare.
In most of these settlements, houses sit just a few metres from rivers. Some people, including Shikoli, live on the slopes of the river itself due to the constant expansion of the settlements. When flash floods occur, these houses are swept away, endangering the lives of their occupants.
Nairobi's drainage system hasn't been upgraded to deal with the rapid growth in the population and infrastructure over the decades
"The existing drainage system was developed 30 years ago to cater for a population of about 2.5 million residents but we're dealing with about 7 million in the daytime and 5.5 million night-time," Simiyu says.
He adds that investment of up to $192m (£143m) is needed to upgrade the sewerage and drainage system entirely.
But there is little sign that either the cash-strapped national or city council will able to raise this kind of money.
The Nairobi River Basin Regeneration programme, a government programme aimed at restoring the city's rivers, found that settlements near rivers, and where there is weak enforcement of regulations, have increased flooding risks. It recommended a "buffer" to protect rivers and "humane relocation" of communities where necessary.
However, rising poverty has driven many people to live close to rivers.
"Our worst case scenario looking at low-income settlements is that up to about 100,000 people are at risk," Simiyu says. "Moderate projections is about 5,000 households or about 20,000 people may be at risk."
Anyone forced to leave their homes will be relocated to 167 designated holding grounds where a stockpile of relief food and supplies will be distributed, Simiyu says.
Nobody knows exactly when the rains will come – or how much rain there will be.
But Kenya's meteorological department warns that November is usually the peak rainfall month of the short rainy season, which normally lasts from October to December.
A regional forecast from the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (Igad) warned in September that there was "an 81% probability of a very strong El Niño during October–December 2026".
So far, the heavy rains predicted have not occurred but experts remain concerned.
In East Africa, this El Niño is being widely compared to a similar weather event in 1997-1998 which caused widespread flooding and destruction in Somalia and Kenya.
Weather forecaster Jemima Gacheru tells the BBC that's because temperature conditions in the Indian Ocean in the 1997 El Niño and those recorded now are similar. This interaction, she says, has been seen to result in very strong rainfall.
"For this season we have a very strong El Niño already in play in the Pacific and then we have a positive Indian Ocean dipole," Gacheru said. This is often called the "Indian Niño" because of its similarity to its Pacific equivalent andrefers to the difference in sea-surface temperatures in opposite parts of the Indian Ocean.
"We expect to have some enhanced rainfall over several parts of the country."
The UN's migration body the International Organization for Migration (IOM) has warned that almost 900,000 people could be forced to leave their homes in Kenya this year, mostly because of the predicted floods.
Dozens of people died in floods in Kenya earlier this year
Kenya is not the only African country worried about the potential impact of El Niño.
In neighbouring Somalia, the country's disaster management agency has warned that 1.2 million people are at risk of displacement caused by extreme weather – including the risk of both floods and drought.
The 1998 floods killed 2,000 people in Somalia and forced a further 250,000 to flee their homes, according to the Food and Agriculture Organisation. Up to 80% of crops were destroyed in some parts of the country.
The United Nation's famine warning system IPC has warned of the increased risk of food insecurity in Somalia due to supply chain issues exacerbated by the impact of El Niño.
Elsewhere on the continent forecasters fear El Niño could bring extreme heat and prolonged periods without rain.
It could cause a crisis for farmers across parts of West Africa, including the semi-arid Sahel region south of the Sahara, as well as in southern parts of the continent, where the risk of crop failure is high.
There are fears El Niño's impact will worsen existing issues.
Communities like Kibera are already grappling with poor housing and rampant poverty, while parts of Somalia are already in the middle of a devastating drought.
National governments in many countries are doing what they can to prepare but the extent of El Niño's impact is impossible to predict.
Back in Kibera, Shikoli and her family are preparing for the worst.
Council officials have told them they should leave their home on the riverbank until the rainy season has passed but Shikoli makes just $2 (£1.5) a day selling groundnuts and fruit from a small stall next to the river.
"I want to move," she says. "But I don't have the means.
"We just have to persevere and leave it to God."

title: Poundland hopeful for last-minute rescue deal to stave off collapse
summary: The BBC understands the discount chain, which has been edging towards administration, will be given more time to find a buyer.
body:
Poundland and its 11,000 employees are hopeful that the retailer's impending collapse can be delayed to allow time for a last-minute rescue deal.
The discount chain has been edging towards administration after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts.
A deadline to secure a buyer for the business is set to expire at midnight, but sources close to the situation have told the BBC that they expect more time will be given, thanks to the release of £10m in funding.
A committee of MPs is set to question Gordon Brothers, Poundland's US owners, on Wednesday following accusations that the investment firm hopes to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 stores and stock piecemeal.
Gordon Brothers - which bought the chain for just £1 last year - is accused of forcing that outcome by restricting Poundland's access to available cash needed to restock stores and pay wages and rent, ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period.
The investment firm has denied the claims.
But pressure remains on Poundland's owners after a takeover bid was rejected. The decision prompted calls for answers from politicians, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
About £50m had been frozen by Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning Poundland bosses were unable to restock shelves across its 600 shops.
However, sources close to the matter told the BBC on Tuesday that a release of £10m by its owners, while "small in the scale of things" could help at least postpone the chain's collapse while a longer term solution was explored.
The 10-day moratorium to protect Poundland from its creditors expires on Thursday, but if there is a prospect of a solvent deal, the deadline could be extended.
Views on the chain's performance differ between those running operations and the owners.
Poundland boss Barry Williams told staff last week that like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4%. The sales period included Halloween, but Williams said this was £1.5m ahead of budget.
He added the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where there were losses of £68m.
However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading".
There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up Poundland stores which could mean continuing employment for workers in the event the chain is broken up and sold off in chunks.
The main issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland as a national chain.

title: Stickers and building sets help drive toy sales ahead of Christmas rush
summary: A bumper year so far for toy sales comes as debate intensifies over screen time and tech connectivity.
body:
Traditional games and stickers are helping to drive a bumper year for toy sales, figures show.
The data comes ahead of the crucial Christmas run-in for retailers, which peaks at 23 toys sold every second in the UK.
The number of toys sold up to October was 17% higher than the same period last year and growth is at a 10-year high, according to research company Circana.
The increase comes despite consumers' cost-of-living pressures, and there are signs that some of the biggest growth in sales is for toys priced between £5 and £10.
Despite relatively low sales in recent years, the toy sector has been buoyed by sales to "kidults".
The kidult market - which is toys and games for those aged over 12 - has been growing, particularly as adults buy toys for themselves.
This growth has continued with a 22% increase in the value of sales in the first half of the year.
But Melissa Symonds, UK toys director at Circana, said that toys for children - which still represents the majority of sales - had recorded a good year so far.
Growing public debate around children's screen time and the role of technology meant squishy toys, stickers and building sets such as Lego were popular.
"Connected toys account for less than 1% of market sales, showing that traditional, hands-on play remains overwhelmingly popular," she said.
Concerns have been raised about the suitability of some connected devices.
ABBC investigation foundan AI teddy marketed as being "perfect" for children as young as three said "I can't help with killing you" after seemingly mishearing a question.
Meanwhile, debate has intensified about keeping youngstersfree from smartphones during the school day.
One in five parents of children aged three to nine say the chance to play together as a family influences what they buy, according to market intelligence company The Insights Family.
Paul Reader, who chairs the Dream Toys selection panel of retailers and experts across the sector, said that parents wanted to engage with their children's play.
"Nothing beats a board game with that. Nothing beats a bit of interaction," he said.
The panel he chairs has selected a list of toys that retailers believe will be some of the most popular this year.
It includes variations on popular toys of recent years, including slime, a soft tiger that roars and grows, and a shark that breaks out of an egg.
Symonds said that, despite rising sales in the year so far, nearly half of toy sales came in the build-up to Christmas, and families were still looking closely at costs.
There was significant growth in toys priced between £5 and £10, she said.
Reader also urged anyone looking for a bargain to shop around, but to ensure that toys were bought from reputable traders so they were genuine and safe.

title: Nvidia hires major US law firm to investigate alleged Chinese spy affair
summary: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.
body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has become the face of the US AI boom
Nvidia has hired one of the largest law firms in the US to investigate the affair between its own chief executive and an alleged Chinese spy.
Jensen Huang, who co-founded the tech company, has admitted to having a romantic relationship outside of his marriage. The woman, Alice Huang, is alleged to be a spy for Beijing.
Nvidia said on Tuesday that it had hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, and that its attorney Joon Kim would lead "a thorough and independent investigation". The FBI is alsoconducting its own probe.
The company's share price has fallen almost to a yearly low, with $500bn (£375bn) wiped of its stock market value since Friday.
Nvidia is widely considered one of the most important companies behind the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, given it is the sole manufacturer of a computer chip used in AI tools.
It is the world's second most valuable company after Apple and its chips have become a matter of national security for US officials who are keen to win the AI race.
Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, and is not related to Jensen Huang, was an executive at Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has been a customer of Nvidia.
Megaspeed had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia has said was investigated and debunked.
Nvidia has also maintained that the US government did not inform it that Megaspeed posed an intelligence concern.
What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
Zoe Kleinman: Nvidia CEO's affair will cause ripples across US and beyond
According to the New York Times, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington earlier this year warning that Jensen Huang was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
Beijing has rejected claims that the Nvidia chief has been targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "intended to smear and malign China".
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that he had spoken to Jensen Huang, who had said he had "no idea she was a spy." Trump said he believed him.
However, the relationship has drawn more political attention. Congressional leaders of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs have asked Huang to appear next week for a closed door briefing.
The Nvidia boss has yet to say whether he will attend, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC. The committee has the authority to subpoena Huang, effectively forcing him to appear before it, if deemed necessary.
When announcing on Sunday that itwould investigatethe affair, Nvidia's board said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised.
It added that a committee of independent directors would oversee the probe.
Watch: Who is suspected Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia affair investigation?
Wachtell is one of the largest law firms in the US and has several notable clients in the tech industry. Among them are OpenAI and Salesforce.
Joon Kim is a former US Attorney for New York's Southern District and spent several years working as a government attorney focusing on fraud and other criminal acts.
The Nvidia investigation will likely be treated as urgent, according to sources familiar with the matter, as Jensen Huang's public image is tightly intertwined with the company.
He has become a key public figure in the development on AI, arguing the technology is a "new industrial revolution" and is on par with the advent of electricity.
It is unclear, however, if Wachtell will be able to interview Alice Huang.
A spokesperson for Nvidia declined to comment on Tuesday when asked if Jensen Huang had retained any of his own legal representation amid the company investigation and the separate one launched by the FBI.

title: Claude chatbot maker set for $1.3tn stock market debut despite 'catastrophic' AI warning
summary: The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78, which is lower than what was expected.
body:
Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) company behind the Claude chatbot, could be valued at around $1.3 trillion (£1 trillion) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange.
The loss-making company says it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each and will raise up to $64bn when it floats this month.
It would value Anthropic at between $1.1tn and $1.3tn which, although large, is below the $2tn some backers of the firm predicted in summer, according to the Financial Times.
The huge valuation comes despite the company warning last month thatAI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity".
It is floating at a volatile time for big tech firms. After last week's US midterm elections, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns a Democrat-led Congress could slow development of AI and the buildout of data centres.
There are also wider fears over the billions of dollars being spent on AI and whether it will pay off.
In its most recent results for the six months to the end of June, Anthropic's revenues jumped to $16.2bn from $1.1bn in the same period last year.
However, its pre-tax loss jumped to $80.7bn from $12.9bn.
Fiona Cincotta, a senior market analyst at City Index, said the $64bn Anthropic wants to raise is "fairly bullish" within "the volatility [and] concerns towards AI that we've seen in sort of particularly last week".
She told Reuters: "It's showing that they are still sort of upbeat about the outlook as far as AI is concerned and that obviously that they think that the demand is going to be there."
Anthropic, which will list under the symbol ANT on 19 November, will be the first fully AI-focused company to go public, making it a test case for the future of the technology.
At $1.3tn, Anthropic's possible valuation is below SpaceX, Elon Musk's rocket, satellite and artificial intelligence company, which listed its shares in June and was valued at nearly $1.8tn.
Global stocks plunge as fears over US AI slowdown spread to Asia and Europe
Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know
Anthropic is just five years old. It was co-founded in 2021 by brother and sister Dario and Daniela Amodei along with five others – all of whom worked at OpenAI, the rival AI giant behind ChatGPT.
It announced its intention to list on the stock market in June and OpenAI followed suit. That listing is now expected to occur early next year.
The listing announcements were followed by a series of incidents involving AI agents, which are bots designed to operate somewhat autonomously, going rogue.
Current and former staff of both companies have warned AI technology was being developed without the ability to protect humanity from possible future harms enacted by AI.
Anthropic has admitted that advanced AI systems "could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponised, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy".
The company has reiterated promises to develop AI to be beneficial to people.
It has warned investors its future success depends largely on its ability to develop the most advanced AI models, and that "any failure to do so could adversely affect our business".

title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
summary: Sales of essential goods such as hand sanitiser soar after the government called on households to be prepared for emergencies.
body:
Sales of essential goods such as bottled water and canned food soared in the 10 days following the launch of the government's "Be Ready" emergency preparedness campaign on 22 October, research indicates.
Hand sanitiser sales were up 83%, sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods climbed 37%, according to data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator.
The government'spublic awareness campaignencouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks.
However, Worldpanel said that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying.
The government campaign encouraged people to keep three days-worth of food and water in their homes.
Wet wipes, a torch and cash were also recommended.
After the campaign launch, the equivalent of an extra 400,000 people per day bought tinned meat, Worldpanel said, although the typical amount remained at 500g, which suggests a gradual stocking-up.
"Shoppers clearly took notice of the 'Be Ready' campaign, but this wasn't panic buying, with less than a third of households buying bottled water in October," said Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel by Numerator.
"Growth came from more people adding the recommended items on the government's checklist to their weekly shop, not from shoppers piling their trolleys high, which is very much in line with what the government wanted households to do," he said.
Sales of tinned and jarred goods rose from £58.2m in the 10 days to 2 November 2025 to £79.5m over the same period in 2026.

title: Tories pledge to cut benefits for children with 'milder cases' of ADHD
summary: Conservative shadow minister Helen Whately says the system risks putting children on a "conveyor belt" towards a "lifetime on benefits".
body:
The Conservatives have pledged to save £2.8bn a year by ending Disability Living Allowance (DLA) payments to families of children with "milder cases" of behavioural disorders, learning difficulties or ADHD.
The policy is one of a series of measures which the party says will save £36bn from the welfare budget.
Shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said the system risked putting children on a "conveyor belt" towards a "lifetime on benefits".
Labour described the Tories' plan as a "charter for homelessness and human misery that would push people into hardship and end up costing the state more".
DLA for children allows parents to claim between £30.30 and £194.60 per week to help cover the additional costs that come with raising a disabled child.
The child must either have difficulty getting about or need more looking after than a child of the same age who does not have a disability.
The Conservatives say child DLA is the "fastest growing benefit in the UK's welfare system", citing government statistics showing the number of cases had risen from  521,476 in 2020 to 914,000.
The party is proposing that in cases where a claim is for a behavioural disorder, learning difficulty or ADHD, only those with the highest need will be eligible for cash payments.
Under the party's plans, those with the most severe conditions, representing around 30% of cases, would continue to receive payments.
The remaining 70% would lose the money but instead receive support through mental health services and family hubs, into which the Conservatives have said they will invest £1bn.
The changes would apply to new claims and reassessments. Those with physical disabilities would be exempt.
The party's other previously-announced cuts include:
£13.7bn from changes to sickness and disability benefits including restricting payments to claimants with "milder mental health issues and neurodiversity conditions such as anxiety, depression and ADHD"
£9.5bn by making it harder for foreign nationals to claim benefits
£4.5bn by reducing local housing allowance payments
£3.1bn by reintroducing the two-child benefit cap
£1bn from tackling fraud
Setting out the party's plans, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said: "The reality is that millions of people can and do contribute to our economy, to their families, to their communities even when they face serious challenges.
"Double amputees run marathons. People who are housebound do wonderful creative work from home. People with autism run some of the biggest tech companies in the world.
"If you tell a young person that their ADHD means they are defective and will never amount to anything, that mindset is likely to be more destructive to their future than the condition itself."
What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?
How a rise in ADHD benefits claims is adding to welfare spending challenge

The Labour government has said it wants to bring the benefits bill down but has not set out a timetable for any reductions.
More details of its plans are expected to come after former minister Alan Milburn has published his review on young people not in education, employment and training.
Both Milburn's review and a review into disability benefits, co-chaired by Minister Sir Stephen Timms, will be published in November.
Asked about Milburn's review, Whately said he was "rolling the pitch for more welfare spending" adding: "We're in no question and no doubt that you can make savings from welfare - it's just that Labour doesn't want to do that."
A Labour Party spokesperson said: "The Conservatives designed and implemented this benefit system, which has driven large numbers of people to be signed off and written off.
"Labour is tackling the collapse in face-to-face assessments, bringing in personalised employment support for sick and disabled people and spreading opportunity to young people through the Youth Guarantee."
The Child Poverty Action Group said: "These proposals would take the UK back to the dark ages, causing the biggest overnight increase in child poverty since records began."
Liberal Democrat Treasury spokesperson Daisy Cooper said: "Until the Conservatives face up to the damage their botched Brexit deal has done, they will remain an out-of-touch, anti-growth, anti-business party, and it will be disabled people and children growing up in poverty who will pay the price."

title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP
summary: Josh Babarinde's proposal is also supported by other MPs, including David Lammy and Sir James Cleverly.
body:
The next census should include more ethnicity options to allow people to define themselves as black English or Asian English, according to a group of MPs.
Liberal Democrat MP Josh Babarinde told the BBC that "most people" in the country believe "you don't have to be white to be English", as he called for the categories to be updated in a similar way to changes in Wales and Scotland.
At the 2021 census, the ethnic group section saw English offered only within the white category.
Babarinde's proposal, dubbed the "St George's Bill", aims to broaden the options and its supporters include Labour's David Lammy and Conservative Sir James Cleverly. It was tabled in the House of Commons on Tuesday.
In his speech to introduce his private member's bill (PMB), Babarinde told MPs he is a "proud Englishman" and has "proud Nigerian heritage".
He said: "But my parents and I were born in England, we grew up in England, our home is in England, yet some voices attempt to reduce Englishness to a skin colour and to a bloodline.
"Well, if we're going to go down that path, my mum's side of the family has been English for as far back as we have traced."
The Eastbourne MP said he had received "death threats for daring to say that you don't have to be white to be English".
He added "English ethnicity is real" before arguing it is a "matter of historical fact that it has never been one bloodline" and "even our Royal Family has German roots".
"Is the King not English either, I ask."
Addressing the ethnicity section of the census, Babarinde said the "only box that says English sits under the white category".
He added: "If you are black, the form offers you black British, if you are Asian, it offers you Asian British, but not English.
"Now, the same question in the Welsh census offers a black Welsh category. In Scotland, the census offers Scottish Asian, for example.
"Yet the best that England offers in our census is a miscellaneous write-in box that may as well be the margin."
Lammy, a former deputy prime minister, said in a statement: "It is quite absurd that neither I or my mixed heritage children can describe themselves as black or mixed race and English on our census form.
"I have long campaigned for us to change to the position enjoyed by others in Wales and Scotland.  We have to end this backward racial gatekeeping."
Babarinde told the BBC he had brought forward the PMB because there were "some corners of our politics who are attempting to gatekeep Englishness for people who are a particular colour".
He also said there are "people like Suella Braverman who have really undermined and questioned the Englishness of people like me".
In 2025, Braverman - then a Conservative MP before her defection to Reform UK -wrote in the Daily Telegraph,externalthat she was British Asian but said she "cannot claim to be English" despite being born and educated in England.
In recent weeks, Braverman has reaffirmed her position andwrote on X,external: "To say I'm English is to take a 'laissez-faire, anything-goes' attitude to ethnicity, citizenship and identity. It also denies me my Asian heritage."
She also said "Englishness is an ethnicity", adding: "There have been English people for centuries and we need to recognise this more if we are to start taking a more muscular approach to citizenship and nationality. And no, it's not racist to say this."
Babarinde introduced his PMB to the Commons using the 10-minute rule process.
This gave him up to 10 minutes to make the case for why he wanted to introduce his PMB.
No MP took up the option to make a 10-minute speech opposing it.
Babarinde asked for his PMB, formally known as the English Ethnic Identity (census particulars) Bill, to return to the Commons on 23 April 2027 - St George's Day - for its second reading debate.
But it is unlikely to be considered further in its current form due to a lack of parliamentary time.
PMBs allow MPs to raise issues they believe ministers should be considering and to develop campaigns showing the strength of support for their ideas.

title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England
summary: The government says it is strengthening its guidance for schools in England, which came into force in June.
body:
Pupils will not be allowed access to their phones at all during the school day under stricter government guidance in England.
Statutory guidance came into force in June, making schools and trusts legally responsible for being phone-free throughout the day.
Ministers now say changes to that guidance will go beyond the current "no see, no hear" policies in place in some schools - where phones can remain in pupils' bags if they are not seen or heard - when it comes into force from September 2027.
But head teachers' unions said schools would struggle to implement stricter new policies without additional funding from government.
Education Secretary Lucy Powell said the government's "clear message" to parents and pupils was that "school is for learning and friendship, not scrolling".
Access to phones "risks pulling children away from their learning and from each other", the government said.
Schools will be able to decide how to follow the guidance. Some schools have invested insealed pouchesor secure lockers. Others collect phones at the start of the day, or have prohibited them from sites altogether.
Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Powell said such policies could achieve a "whole-school culture change" - and that was "what we want to see happening everywhere".
Karl Harrison, head teacher at Burnage Academy for Boys in Manchester, told the programme the school had spent £20,000 to bring in a system of metal detectors and phone pouches to prevent pupils from accessing their phones.
While some felt their freedom had gone, locking phones away had increased how much pupils socialised at school, he said.
"People now can talk to each other, instead of scrolling on a device," he said.
"It's also increased levels of focus in lessons because now there's less distraction, and people are achieving higher grades."
Some schools - like Brownhills Ormiston Academy, in the West Midlands - provide pupils with lockable pouches for their phones
Paul Whiteman, general secretary of the NAHT school leaders union, said phones could raise "safety issues" and be an "unhelpful distraction" during the school day. But he said the more robust measures recommended under the new guidance would "come at a cost".
Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said the latest guidance "does at least provide some clarity", but added that school leaders "cannot simply make mobile phones disappear".
"If all schools are going to be expected to have lockable pouches or other secure storage facilities for every pupil, the cost involved will be very significant indeed," he said.
"This is not feasible unless the government puts in the funding required to meet these costs."
Responding to questions about funding, Powell told BBC Breakfast that she wanted heads to have the autonomy to implement the policies that work best for their schools.
Dame Rachel de Souza, Children's Commissioner for England, said she welcomed strong action to stop phones distracting pupils and disrupting the school day.
Charlotte Ashton, co-founder of campaign group of Generation Focus, similarly welcomed the changes, saying "no see, no hear" policies were not working and pupils were still "TikToking in the toilets".
"Ultimately, we need to get to a point where it's not normal for every single child to have a personal internet-enabled device in their pockets with them 24/7," she said.
A smartphone ban in English schools is coming into force. What's changing?
Parents want to ban smartphones in schools, but there's one reason they're worried
Shadow Education Secretary Laura Trott said she was "delighted that Labour have finally listened to us and agreed to properly ban smartphones in schools".
She said it was also the "right thing to do" to have a review of safety standards around the technology used in schools, which the government has also announced on the back ofcalls for improved guidance.
But she criticised what she called a lack of "joined up thinking" over what new tech was being allowed in classrooms.
Because education is devolved, the approach to phones in schools varies across the UK.
InScotland,external, the government has said it will introduce a new law to restrict the personal use of phones in schools, and launched a consultation on the issue over the summer.
InWales,external, the Senedd recently voted against a motion to introduce a national statutory ban on phones in classrooms. The Welsh government launched a 12-week consultation in September, which it says will shape its guidance to support schools in developing a mobile phone policy.
Schools are still encouraged to restrict the use of phones during the school day, but heads have flexibility over how to implement their own rules.
And inNorthern Ireland, Education Minister Paul Givan launched a 12-week consultation in August on whether to ban mobile phones from schools by law, calling for "a stronger and more consistent approach across our education system".
Rules around phones in schools are separate from the UK'supcoming ban on social mediafor under-16s, due to be introduced in March.
Children will be barred from accessing platforms like Instagram, Snapchat and TikTok. Vinted and eBay could also be included in the list of platforms set to be banned, the culture secretary has said.

title: Scottish Labour leader says the UK should re-join EU
summary: Michael Marra said he wanted "solidarity, not separation" and accepted that "re-joining the EU won't be easy".
body:
Michael Marra said getting back in the EU should be a "long-term objective"
The Scottish Labour leader has called for the UK to re-join the European Union, insisting it should be a "long-term objective" for the whole country.
During his first major speech since becoming party leader, Michael Marra said he wanted "solidarity, not separation" and accepted that "re-joining the EU won't be easy".
Marra acknowledged there would be "serious questions" over issues such as currency and borders before the UK could return to the EU.
Last month, the UK government ruled out re-joining the EU within this parliament but Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he wanted toexplore closer tieswith Europe.
The UK Labour leader suggested another referendum on the issue could feature in a future Labour manifesto.
Speaking at the University of Edinburgh, Marra said: "The UK should re-join the European Union and Scottish Labour will work to make that happen.
"I don't pretend it will happen quickly. But I believe we should set it as a long-term objective for the UK and that Scotland should lead the change in making that happen."
Andy Burnham will be travelling to Brussels next week where he is expected to sign a series of deals with the EU
Marra accepted his call goes further than Prime Minister Andy Burnham's position.
He added: "Re-joining the EU is not the current policy of the UK Labour Party and not the current policy of the UK government.
"The UK Labour Party isn't there yet. This is a distinct Scottish Labour position."
Marra's predecessor, Anas Sarwar, had pushed for closer ties with the EU after Brexit but did not go as far as to call for the UK to re-join the bloc.
"It is in Scotland's interests, and in the interests of the whole United Kingdom, for the UK to re-join the European Union," added Marra.
Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride
UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
Why the prime minister wants to talk about Brexit again
Addressing party supporters, Marra set out how going back into Europe would boost the economy.
The North East MSP said that "breaking down barriers" with European nations would "help Scottish businesses grow, attract investment and create better-paid jobs".
It could also "help bring down prices and generate more money for our public services", he added.
Marra accepted that re-joining the EU "won't solve every problem we have", but added: "If we're serious about growth, we cannot keep ignoring the opportunity on our doorstep."
His speech came ahead of the prime minister travelling to Brussels next week where he is expected to sign a series of deals with the EU.
These will be focused on bringing down post-Brexit trade barriers on food and farming, as well as working more closely on emissions trading and making it easier for young people from the UK to work, live and study in Europe, and vice versa.
Responding to Marra's speech, SNP deputy leader Keith Brown said: "Having accepted that people are able to revisit the EU referendum decision taken 10 years ago, how can any Labour Party politician now seriously claim Scotland can't revisit the independence referendum decision taken 12 years ago?"
Marra told BBC Scotland News that he did not support a second referendum, and said he believed the people of Scotland did not either.
Scottish Liberal Democrats leader Alex Cole-Hamilton said he was pleased to see Scottish Labour following his party's lead.
He added: "It's important to offer the people of Britain a realistic roadmap back to Europe. That starts with re-joining the single market and establishing a customs union as a key first step."
The Scottish Greens' co-leader Gillian Mackay said she agrees with Marra that Scotland's "place is in the EU" - but added it was hypocritical to support this while ignoring "growing demand" for an Independence referendum.
Scottish Conservative leader Russell Findlay said people in Scotland were "sick of constant constitutional uncertainty" and want "politicians to focus on the cost-of-living, cutting taxes and fixing public service".
Reform UK Scotland's Max Bannerman said the country does not need to re-join the EU to see growth.
Michael Marra has set a very clear policy direction for his party. So why now?
Andy Burnham took the first step by taking his tin opener to this can of political worms at the Labour Party conference as he seeks closer ties with the EU.
There's a crunch summit in Brussels a week on Friday.
But Marra is going further than the prime minister.
He points out rejoining the EU is not the current policy of the UK government and that this is a distinct, Scottish Labour position.
Marra is a new leader and he needs to make the news with a stand-out position, so that also helps to answer the "why now" question.
Scottish Labour believe their leader has two clear roles; challenge the Scottish government and influence the UK government.
Marra thinks he can be influential and it's a change even from the position he held when he took over as leader.
There may be a fair amount of Scottish public support for this and brings Labour alongside the SNP as they both burnish their pro-EU credentials.
Labour and the SNP will continue their traditional battle and now Marra has a new fight on his hands to fully convince his party of his stance as he demands "rejoin" be included in their next general election manifesto.
